name: Barth across the Sahara and the Sahel
summary: A British-funded mission sets out from Tripoli; its leader and its other German member die, and Heinrich Barth carries on alone for five years, from Aïr to Bornu, Adamawa, Sokoto and Timbuktu. He learned the languages, copied the chronicles, and wrote the fullest account of the Sahel and its history that Europe would have for a century.

stops.note: The mission of James Richardson, Heinrich Barth and Adolf Overweg sets out.
The city of the Aïr mountains.
The great market city of Hausaland.
The capital of Bornu, by Lake Chad; Richardson has died on the way.
South to Adamawa, where he crosses the upper Benue.
The capital of the caliphate; Overweg has died, and Barth goes on alone.
Seven months in the city under the protection of Sheikh al-Bakkai.
Back at Bornu, he meets Eduard Vogel, sent out because Barth was thought dead.
Across the desert to the coast.
